::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 10 [1899]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/88
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd)
Thank you for Crispin  I was glad of him for we are feeding [Alethea](people/person_182.qmd)with light literature, she having broken down, with nothing the matter but a course of overwork after the influenza-  first the children’s measles, then going to Holmwood to lodgings with the children, no nursery maid, and the lady nurse not looking after her, or doing nursery maid’s work and then a good deal to do at homecoming, mission and guests.  So she is to take a great rest, and to go to Dorking alone when [Frances](people/person_1604.qmd) goes home.  She left Torquay yesterday for the [Hallidays](people/person_616.qmd) at Taunton.  I do not think you should get pledged to [Chwoman](organizations/other_64.qmd), but oh! if you could get hold of G L, or something of the sort.  It was such a useless story in G L and very sad besides.

[SPCK](organizations/other_40.qmd) as far as I have read is improved.  [Wells Gardiner](organizations/other_114.qmd) only ordered six dozen [Doves in E. Nest](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd) so [Macmillan](people/person_111.qmd) concluded it was not worth his while  30 000 must be ordered to make a /6 ed answer!  I don’t think he took into account the numbers who order things through their own bookseller or the stations.  He would have printed it if 15 000 had been expected.  I am afraid the local people only say ‘Out of print[‘] and don’t send the orders.

Tipper Moor was the name of the battle I could not remember![^1]  Would not Mungo be a good name  He was St Kentigern but is better known as Mungo Park! and I don’t think the name has much been taken.  My little Skye who died I meant to be Cormac, but [Annie Cazenove](people/person_274.qmd) having apparently never heard of the [Lord of the Isles](other_books/otherbook_747.qmd), read it Carmac and spoilt it-  where it means a charioteer and Mungo means pleasant.

The [Guardian](organizations/other_75.qmd) never sends me [Nat Soc](organizations/other_32.qmd) books, but lots of SPCK.  [Vanity and Vexation](other_books/otherbook_748.qmd) is of the young lady order, and not at all bad, not a novellette[^2]  I flatter myself that severity was wholesome

your affectionate
C M Yonge

You will like to see what [Mrs Mitchell](people/person_1007.qmd) says.

---

[^1]: Perhaps the battle of Tippermuir (1644)?
[^2]: CMY had evidently written a review of A.E.D., *Vanity and Vexation* (London, SPCK 1899), presumably in the *Guardian*, fairly recently.
